title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Black Economy Taskforce Measures No. 2) Bill 2018
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Black Economy Taskforce Measures No. 2) Bill 2018

speeches.speaker: Christopher Pyne
speeches.brief: The speaker listed three bills: the Treasury Laws Amendment (Making Sure Multinationals Pay Their Fair Share of Tax in Australia and Other Measures) Bill 2018, the Treasury Laws Amendment (Black Economy Taskforce Measures No. 2) Bill 2018, and the Excise Tariff Amendment (Collecting Tobacco Duties at Manufacture) Bill 2018.

speeches.speaker: Stuart Robert
speeches.brief: The bill alters the Excise Tariff Act 1921 to enable duty calculation after moving the taxing point, as part of a package implementing Black Economy Taskforce recommendations to disrupt the illicit tobacco market and stop tobacco leakage from warehouses.

speeches.speaker: Steven Ciobo
speeches.brief: The Customs Amendment (Collecting Tobacco Duties at the Border) Bill 2018 will require importers to pay all tobacco duties at the border from 1 July 2019, aiming to prevent criminal groups from accessing duty-free tobacco. The bill is part of a package with two other bills targeting tobacco duty collection at manufacture.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: The government's return to surplus is based on an accounting change that shifts $3.27 billion into the 2019-20 tax year by taxing tobacco 12 weeks earlier upon entry into Australia, rather than when it leaves the warehouse.

speeches.speaker: Tim Wilson
speeches.brief: The speaker argued the Treasury Laws Amendment (Black Economy Taskforce Measures No. 2) Bill 2018 is constructive, aiming to increase tax compliance and close loopholes, while criticising the opposition for lacking economic credibility and obstructing budget repair.

speeches.speaker: Milton Dick
speeches.brief: Gross debt has reached a record $540.1 billion and net debt has doubled under the Liberal-National government, while Labor supports the black economy measures but criticises a tobacco tax timing trick used to bring forward a budget surplus. Labor also calls for stronger action on tax havens, proposing reforms including mandatory disclosure of foreign residency and beneficial ownership.

speeches.speaker: David Coleman
speeches.brief: The government announced measures from the 2018-19 budget to combat the black economy, including denying tax deductions for payments where employers fail withholding and reporting obligations, extending taxable payment reporting to the road freight, security and IT industries, and changing the point at which tobacco is taxed to combat illicit tobacco. These changes aim to restore tax integrity and support Australia's tobacco control policies.
